Agent Name: Planner
, Step Number: 3
, Reason for Mistake: In Step 3, the Planner incorrectly deduced that Albert I is the paternal grandfather. The Planner reasoned: "Albert IV -> father: John II -> father: Albert II -> father: Albert I. Therefore, paternal grandfather of Albert IV should be Albert I". This logic is flawed because it skips a generation. If Albert II is the father of Albert IV (which is false, Albert II is the father of John II), then Albert I would be the grandfather. However, the correct lineage is Albert IV (child) -> John II (father) -> Albert II (grandfather). Albert I is the great-grandfather. The Planner failed to correctly identify that the "paternal grandfather" is the father of the subject's father (John II's father is Albert II), not the father of the subject's grandfather. The Planner confused the generation count, leading to the wrong answer (Albert I instead of Albert II).
